context: Renewal call. Customer: Pine Ridge Clinics, contact Alina Brandt, operations lead. Current contract: 80 seats at $14,000 per year, renews on 1 March. Our usual discount cap on renewals is 5 percent without approval.

lines.text: Hi Alina, thanks for joining. I see Sam from finance is here as well.

lines.speaker: Alina
lines.text: Yes, Sam will keep an eye on the numbers.
Good. Let us start with your situation today.

lines.speaker: Alina
lines.text: We have grown a lot, we are around a hundred and twenty seats now.
That is a big change from the eighty in the contract. I will check the usage report.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Our budget for this tool next year is nine thousand dollars, no more.
Noted, I will take that into account.

lines.speaker: Alina
lines.text: Last quarter we lost forty percent of our new staff accounts in the first week because nobody finished onboarding.
That is a high number and onboarding is the first place I would look.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: The renewal is on the first of March and we will not sign anything before the audit ends on the fifteenth.
Then the dates collide, so I will think about an extension.

lines.speaker: Alina
lines.text: Support tickets doubled since January, from about fifty to a hundred a month.
That fits with the growth in seats.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Another vendor offered us a flat rate of ten thousand for unlimited seats.
I would like to compare what that flat rate includes.

lines.speaker: Alina
lines.text: It is raining here again and the roads are a mess.
Same here, the traffic was terrible this morning.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I will send you the audit schedule after the call.
